title: 9.4.4 Enzyme Catalysis · Self-Assessment

paras.en: A large number of catalysts called enzymes are found in living tissue[scan obscured] Enzymes are proteins with high molecular weight and act as catalyst[scan obscured] biochemical reactions occurring in all living matter. For example ptyalin[scan obscured] enzyme found in saliva, accelerates the conversion of starch into sugar. Althoug[scan obscured] starch will react with water to form sugar, several weeks will require for th[scan obscured] conversion to occur in the absence of the enzyme. A trace of ptyalin makes th[scan obscured] reaction proceed in minutes at body temperature. Likewise, pepsin in gastric ju[scan obscured] breaks down protein into simpler molecules which can be utilized by body cel[scan obscured] Nearly every step of breakdown of a complex molecule to a series of small[scan obscured] ones, in biological systems, is catalysed by specific enzymes.
